packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

- Single leaf, upright, scale bar at foot (approx. 19 cm visible width). Top edge torn
  and ragged; right edge damaged with a notch about two-thirds down; lower edge worn.
- Two columns of text in a small Gothic book hand, very heavily abbreviated.
  Left column is cut at its left edge (line beginnings lost); right column is complete
  in width.
- A dark rectangular patch (blacked-out/repair or hole) at the head of the right
  column, upper left of that column.
- Red rubric at the top right of the right column, two lines (appears to read
  "De statu ... / religione" -- tentative, to check on the tile).
- Alternating red and blue paragraph marks (pilcrow-type "C" marks) throughout both
  columns; a large decorated initial (blue/red with a long pinkish-violet descender
  running down the left margin of the right column) near the top of the right column.
- Marginal annotations in the right margin: "p(ro)fessio(n)is" (?) near top, a
  pointing hand (manicule) with a word "...heremitas"(?) at mid-height, small notes
  ("c."?) lower down; small marks in the intercolumnar space.
- Tentative interpretation: a continuous prose text with chapter/paragraph divisions
  and frequent short references (numbers, abbreviations) suggestive of citation
  chains; no visible separate commentary block or interlinear gloss on this face.
- Tiles: 002-005 (narrow) appear to cover the left column top to bottom; 006-009
  (wide) the right column top to bottom. Overlap between vertical neighbours expected.
- Face 2 overview is image-010.jpg; tiles 011-018.

SUMMARY OF COVERAGE AND LIMITATIONS
- Face 1 (image-001; tiles 002-009): both columns read line by line top to bottom.
  Right column (006-009, about 70 distinct lines) is the most secure reading: a
  rubricated section opening (rubric ending "religione"), a list of questions
  ("Quis sit regularis, unde dicatur, ad quid teneatur, et qualiter ..., et utrum exire
  possit uel reuocari"), then discussion with dense allegation chains (i(nfra)/s(upra),
  "de ...", c./§./q./di. references). Left column (002-005, about 80 distinct lines) is
  cut at the left, so every line beginning is lost; many readings there are uncertain.
  Visible paragraph openings: "Item p(ro) hac uia" (003-07), "septimodecimo" (004-09).
- Face 2 (image-010; tiles 011-018): left column (011-014) almost entirely abraded;
  only the last ~10 lines (014) give partial readings. One enhanced crop tried
  (crops/011-top-enh.jpg) without benefit. Right column (015-018) is cut at the right
  and stained; partial readings of about 60 lines, with paragraph openings at 015-20
  ("[..]tauodecimo q(ue)ritur"), 016-12 (blue ¶), 016-18 (red ¶ "Q..."), 017-06
  ("[..]nodecimo(?) q(ueritu)r si quis ..."), 018-12 (red ¶).
- Expansions in parentheses are proposals; "(?)" marks uncertain readings. Citation
  abbreviations are given as written with tentative expansions only.
- Suggested follow-up: UV/multispectral imaging for face 2 left column; higher-contrast
  crops of face 1 left column lines 002-01..04 and 002-11..15.
- I did not stop on the image limit; all 18 images were opened.
- Beyond the brief: one enhanced crop of image-011 (allowed: "crops you make of them").
